pages.title: Integrate with Bridge
pages.description: Connect your CRM, automation, or landing page with the REST API, webhooks, and Custom Connections.
pages.contentMarkdown:
Build with your preferred coding tool

## Connect your AI coding assistant

Give your coding tool the current Bridge docs. Choose it below for setup, an example prompt and a connection check.

  [Codex →](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#codex)
  [Claude Code →](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#claude-code)
  [Cursor →](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#cursor)
  [GitHub Copilot →](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#github-copilot)

Docs access needs no Bridge API Key. Workspace access is separate.

## Choose your integration

  

    

### [REST API](https://docs.bridge.new/credentials.md)

      Create contacts, conversations and messages from your server.

      **Access:** server-side `x-api-key`.
    

    

### [Webhooks](https://docs.bridge.new/webhooks.md)

      Receive Bridge events at your HTTPS endpoint.

      **Access:** verify webhook credentials and freshness.
    

    

### [Custom Connections](https://docs.bridge.new/lead-capture/index.md)

      Capture landing-page leads and queue an opening WhatsApp message.

      **Access:** `captureKey` and reCAPTCHA; no REST API Key.
    

  

## Make your first REST API request

  

### Get your API credentials

    Follow [Authentication](https://docs.bridge.new/credentials.md) to generate an API key in the Bridge Admin Console. Ask your Bridge administrator for access if needed. Keep the key on your server.
  

  

### Check the connection

    Use your `x-api-key` header to call the authenticated [health check](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/health/health-check.md) at `https://api-connect-us.bridge.new/bridge/api/health`.

    Continue in the **REST API** tab. Each endpoint lists its fields, responses, and examples.
  

**Note**

  Custom Connections uses a separate endpoint and public `captureKey`. Follow its [integration guide](https://docs.bridge.new/lead-capture/integration.md). A `202` confirms acceptance, not WhatsApp delivery.

## Build from the published contract

- [Create a Contact and send a message](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/first-conversation.md) — follow the complete Contact → conversation → message workflow.
- [Send a PDF or attachment](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/send-attachments.md) — checksum, upload URL, file upload and message.
- [Send a WhatsApp template](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/send-template.md) — discover variables and supply caller-required values.
- [Start Agent outbound and hand off](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/agent-outbound.md) — choose an Agent, understand `forceSend`, reuse and recovery.
- [Create and move pipeline records](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/pipeline-records.md) — create records for existing Contacts, retry with `Idempotency-Key`, avoid lost updates with `expectedRevision`, close and reopen.
- [Look up identifiers](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/identifiers.md) and [page through results](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/pagination.md) — use the right IDs and cursors.
- [Rate limits](https://docs.bridge.new/rate-limits.md) — share the request budget and handle `429` responses.
- [Error codes](https://docs.bridge.new/error-codes.md) — interpret REST API errors. Custom Connections has a separate [error reference](https://docs.bridge.new/lead-capture/errors.md).
- [WhatsApp template parameters](https://docs.bridge.new/templates-and-parameters.md) — open conversations with WhatsApp templates and supply their variables.
- [Changelog](https://docs.bridge.new/changelog.md) — review changes that affect integrations.

Read without MCP using the [trilingual documentation index](https://docs.bridge.new/llms.txt), [English index](https://docs.bridge.new/llms-en.json), [English collection](https://docs.bridge.new/llms-full-en.json), or [integration guidance for AI agents](https://docs.bridge.new/skill.md). Use the exact [REST Integrations OpenAPI](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/openapi.yaml) or [Custom Connections OpenAPI](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/campaign-leads.openapi.yaml) for schemas.

For help using the Bridge application, visit the [Help Center](https://help.bridge.new).

pages.title: Connect your AI coding assistant
pages.description: Connect Codex, Claude Code, Cursor or GitHub Copilot to current Bridge documentation, then build from the exact API contract.
pages.contentMarkdown:
Give your coding assistant access to the current Bridge documentation before asking it to build your integration. Choose your tool below, add the public MCP endpoint, and run the connection check.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Server URL | `https://docs.bridge.new/mcp` |
| Connection | Remote HTTP / Streamable HTTP |
| Suggested local name | `bridgeDocs` |
| Bridge credentials | None for this documentation server |

**Note**

  This connects your assistant to **Bridge documentation**. It does not connect it to your workspace or give it permission to create Contacts or send messages. Your integration uses the separate [REST API credentials](https://docs.bridge.new/credentials.md), or the public [Custom Connections](https://docs.bridge.new/lead-capture/index.md) setup. The documentation server also exposes an optional feedback tool that sends documentation comments to Bridge.

## Choose your coding assistant

  

### [Codex](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#codex)

CLI and local IDE configuration.

  

### [Claude Code](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#claude-code)

One command, then check the connection.

  

### [Cursor](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#cursor)

Add the server to your project's MCP file.

  

### [GitHub Copilot](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#github-copilot)

Guided setup in VS Code or portable project configuration.

## Codex

**Before you start:** have Codex CLI or the Codex IDE extension installed. For the CLI, add the server in your terminal:

```bash
codex mcp add bridgeDocs --url https://docs.bridge.new/mcp
codex mcp list
```

The list should include `bridgeDocs` with the Bridge documentation URL. Listing it confirms configuration; use [the connection check below](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#check-the-connection) to confirm that it can actually read documentation.

If you prefer editing configuration, add this entry to `~/.codex/config.toml`. Keep your other settings and server entries:

```toml
[mcp_servers.bridgeDocs]
url = "https://docs.bridge.new/mcp"
```

Restart the client or extension after changing its configuration. In the Codex terminal interface, `/mcp` shows active servers. Local Codex clients can share configuration on the same host; remote environments can have separate configuration and policy.

**Example prompt:**

> Use bridgeDocs to read the Bridge REST contract and the first-conversation guide. Prepare a Node.js integration that creates a Contact, starts a Conversation and creates a Message. List the required identifiers and configuration first. Keep every API field and type unchanged, cite your sources, and do not make live API requests.

[Official Codex MCP guidance](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli).

## Claude Code

**Before you start:** have Claude Code installed. Add the server to your personal configuration so it is available across projects:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http bridgeDocs --scope user https://docs.bridge.new/mcp
claude mcp list
```

For a shared project configuration instead, use `--scope project` rather than `--scope user`. Review the resulting project configuration before committing it.

Start Claude Code and use `/mcp` to inspect `bridgeDocs`. Then run [the connection check below](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#check-the-connection). The Bridge documentation endpoint does not need a Bridge API Key or an OAuth login.

**Example prompt:**

> Use bridgeDocs to read the current Bridge webhook verification and receiver guides. Implement a Python receiver with the documented HMAC representation and durable acceptance before acknowledgement. Add offline tests using the published signature vector. Explain the timestamp limitation and duplicate handling, and cite the pages you used.

[Official Claude Code MCP guidance](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp).

## Cursor

**Before you start:** open your integration project in Cursor. Create or update `.cursor/mcp.json` in that project. Merge the entry with any existing servers:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bridgeDocs": {
      "url": "https://docs.bridge.new/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

For a personal configuration across projects, use `~/.cursor/mcp.json` instead. In Cursor's **Customize** sidebar, check that the server is enabled. Open an Agent conversation and run [the connection check below](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#check-the-connection); relevant MCP tools appear under **Available Tools**. Review tool requests when Cursor asks.

**Example prompt:**

> Use bridgeDocs to find the complete PDF attachment workflow. Implement a server-side upload that hashes the exact file bytes as Base64 SHA-256, requests a presigned upload, sends the required PUT and creates a Message with the returned mediaId. Preserve the documented fields and explain each stage's failure handling. Do not send a Bridge API Key to the upload URL.

[Official Cursor MCP guidance](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp).

## GitHub Copilot

**Before you start:** enable GitHub Copilot in VS Code and open your project folder. Select **Copilot** as the session target.

1. Open the Command Palette with `Command` + `Shift` + `P` on macOS, or `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `P` on Windows/Linux.
2. Run **MCP: Add Server** and choose **HTTP (HTTP or Server-Sent Events)**.
3. Enter `https://docs.bridge.new/mcp` and name the server `bridgeDocs`.
4. Choose **Global → Copilot Global** for your personal configuration, when available. Review the destination shown by your VS Code version and any server trust request.
5. Open a Copilot conversation, enable the Bridge documentation tools for that session, and run [the connection check below](https://docs.bridge.new/connect-your-agent.md#check-the-connection).

For a shared project using the current portable Copilot configuration, create or merge this entry into `.mcp.json` at the workspace root:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bridgeDocs": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://docs.bridge.new/mcp",
      "tools": ["*"]
    }
  }
}
```

The portable Copilot format above differs from editor-managed `.vscode/mcp.json`, which uses a `servers` object. Use the file for the connection you selected; do not mix the two shapes. If the portable destination is unavailable in your version, use the guided setup and its selected configuration file.

**Example prompt:**

> Use bridgeDocs to read the Custom Connections guide and its separate OpenAPI contract. Prepare a landing-page form that records consent, obtains a new CAPTCHA token for each attempt and shows a 202 as accepted with its requestId. Keep captureKey, request fields and the configured CAPTCHA action unchanged. Do not use a REST API Key in the page.

[Official VS Code setup](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers) · [Copilot configuration reference](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/mcp-configuration).

## Check the connection

Ask this after configuring any of the four clients:

> Use the Bridge documentation MCP server to search for creating a Message. Read the MessageRequest schema from the published REST OpenAPI. Which three fields are required, and does a successful 201 prove WhatsApp delivery? Cite the exact Bridge source you read. Do not call the business API.

A successful check uses a documentation tool and cites a Bridge page or schema. It should identify `conversationId`, `messageBody` and `enableExternalBroadcast` as required. It should distinguish a created Message from a provider delivery receipt. A plausible answer without a tool call or source is not a connection test.

## Read with any AI tool, without MCP

No MCP connection is required to read Bridge documentation. Give an assistant that can fetch URLs the [trilingual documentation index](https://docs.bridge.new/llms.txt), then choose the sources for your task and language:

| Language | Page index | Collected documentation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| English | [English index](https://docs.bridge.new/llms-en.json) | [English collection](https://docs.bridge.new/llms-full-en.json) |
| Español | [Índice en español](https://docs.bridge.new/llms-es.json) | [Documentación en español](https://docs.bridge.new/llms-full-es.json) |
| Português do Brasil | [Índice em português](https://docs.bridge.new/llms-pt-br.json) | [Documentação em português](https://docs.bridge.new/llms-full-pt-br.json) |

The index points to individual `.md` pages and the exact OpenAPI files. The [combined collection](https://docs.bridge.new/llms-full.txt) includes all three languages; a language-specific collection is smaller. Collected endpoint descriptions do not replace the complete schemas in OpenAPI.

The language-specific files use JSON: the index lists page URLs, and each collection provides the page text as Markdown in its `contentMarkdown` field. The general `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` remain plain Markdown.

**Example prompt:**

> Read https://docs.bridge.new/llms.txt and select the English sources for sending a PDF. Read the full attachment guide and the linked REST OpenAPI before writing code. Explain the upload sequence, required fields and delivery limitations. Preserve the published API signatures and cite the URLs you read. Prepare code only; do not make live requests.

If you use MCP search, specify `language: "en"`, `language: "es"` or `language: "pt-BR"` to retrieve the requested language. HTTP exports use `.md`; MCP filesystem page reads use `.mdx`. For a concise capability and source guide, read [Bridge integration guidance](https://docs.bridge.new/skill.md).

## Build with the right contract

The server provides documentation search, complete page/schema reading in a virtual documentation filesystem, and optional documentation feedback. The filesystem tool does not run commands on your computer. Feedback is separate from searching and reading; use it only when you intend to send a documentation comment.

Give your assistant the task and relevant workflow:

- [First conversation](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/first-conversation.md): Contact → Conversation → Message.
- [Attachments](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/send-attachments.md): file bytes → checksum → presigned PUT → Message.
- [Templates](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/send-template.md): discover variables before sending.
- [Agent outbound](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/agent-outbound.md): select an Agent and understand `forceSend`, reuse and recovery.
- [Webhook receiver](https://docs.bridge.new/webhooks/receive-events.md): verify, persist, acknowledge and process.

The [documentation index](https://docs.bridge.new/llms.txt) locates pages. [Collected documentation](https://docs.bridge.new/llms-full.txt) gathers guides and endpoint descriptions; it does not include every schema. Before generating code, read the individual endpoint Markdown or the appropriate [REST OpenAPI](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/openapi.yaml) or [Custom Connections OpenAPI](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/campaign-leads.openapi.yaml).

Ask the assistant to preserve hosts, methods, paths, authentication, identifiers, field names, types, required/nullable fields, enums, defaults, limits and response codes. If published sources conflict, identify the passages and confirm the current behavior before relying on them.

## If the server does not appear

| Symptom | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Server missing | Confirm the file location or configuration scope, the server name and the client/environment you are using. Keep existing configuration when adding the entry. |
| Configured but no tools | Restart or reload the client, enable the server and check its MCP status or logs. A managed organization may restrict custom servers. |
| Authentication prompt | Bridge's public documentation server needs no Bridge API Key. Check the URL and your client's or organization's policy. Do not paste workspace credentials into chat. |
| Answer without citations | Ask explicitly to use `bridgeDocs`, search, and read the endpoint schema. Run the connection check again. |
| MCP temporarily unavailable | Read the [index](https://docs.bridge.new/llms.txt), endpoint Markdown and OpenAPI directly. The documentation server does not have a separate uptime commitment. |

Client interfaces change over time. Setup options can differ by version and organization policy; use the linked provider documentation if your menus differ. Provider instructions last checked: **November 14, 2026**.

pages.title: REST API authentication
pages.description: Generate and use a server-side API key for the REST Integrations API, and keep it separate from webhook credentials and Custom Connections.
pages.contentMarkdown:
## Overview

Every request to the **REST Integrations API** at `https://api-connect-us.bridge.new` uses an **API Key** in the `x-api-key` header. This key identifies your application and authorizes it to access Bridge resources on behalf of your organization.

| Integration surface | Credential handling |
| --- | --- |
| REST Integrations API | Server-side `x-api-key` sent to `https://api-connect-us.bridge.new`. |
| Webhooks | Your receiver checks the configured webhook API key, HMAC signature and freshness policy. Follow [Verify signatures](https://docs.bridge.new/webhooks/verifying-signatures.md). |
| Custom Connections | Browser-side public `captureKey` and reCAPTCHA; no authentication header. Follow its [integration guide](https://docs.bridge.new/lead-capture/integration.md). |

**Note**

  You will need access to Bridge's admin console at https://admin.bridge.new.

  If you don't have one, please ask your Bridge Admin to create you a user.

---

## Generating an API Key

  

### Open the Admin Console

    Go to your [Bridge Dashboard](https://admin.bridge.new) and log in with your credentials.
  

  

### Navigate to API Keys

    In the left panel, go to **Developers → API Keys Management**.
  

  

### Create a new key

    Click **Generate New Key**. You can give it a descriptive name and set an expiration date.

    

**Warning**

      **Important:**\
      Your API Key will only be displayed once upon creation. Copy it immediately and store it in a secure location — you will not be able to retrieve it later.
    

  

---

## Using your API Key

Include your REST API Key in the `x-api-key` header on every request to the REST Integrations host:

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api-connect-us.bridge.new/bridge/api/health" \
  -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY"
```

```javascript
const response = await fetch("https://api-connect-us.bridge.new/bridge/api/health", {
  method: "GET",
  headers: {
    "x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY",
  },
});

const data = await response.json();
console.log(data);
```

```python
import requests

response = requests.get(
    "https://api-connect-us.bridge.new/bridge/api/health",
    headers={"x-api-key": "YOUR_API_KEY"}
)

print(response.json())
```


**Note**

  Use the `GET /bridge/api/health` endpoint to verify that your API Key is valid and your connection is working correctly.

---

## Security Best Practices

- **Use environment variables** — Store your API Key in an environment variable (e.g. `BRIDGE_API_KEY`) instead of hardcoding it in your source code.
- **Never expose keys in client-side code** — API Keys should only be used in server-side applications. Never include them in frontend code, mobile apps, or public repositories.
- **Set an expiration date** — Always configure an expiration when creating a key. Avoid using keys without a defined expiry.
- **One key per application** — Use a separate API Key for each service or application that connects to Bridge. This limits the impact if a key is compromised.
- **Rotate keys periodically** — Create a new key and update your applications before deactivating the old one. This ensures zero downtime during rotation.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Error | Possible Cause | Solution |
| ----- | -------------- | -------- |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Invalid, expired, or missing API Key | Verify that your key is correct, active, and included in the `x-api-key` header |
| `403 Forbidden` | The API Key does not have access to the requested resource | Check that your key has the necessary permissions for this endpoint |
| Cannot retrieve API Key | The key is only shown once at creation time | Generate a new API Key from the Admin Console |

For a complete list of error codes, see the [Error Codes](https://docs.bridge.new/error-codes.md) reference.

---

## Related Topics

- [Error Codes](https://docs.bridge.new/error-codes.md) — Full reference of Bridge API error codes
- [REST API Reference](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/health/health-check.md) — Explore all available endpoints
- [Webhooks](https://docs.bridge.new/webhooks.md) — Set up real-time event notifications

pages.title: Glossary and identifiers
pages.description: Find the correct workspace, Contact, Bridge User, Agent, conversation, template, line, and media identifiers without confusing them.
pages.contentMarkdown:
## Start with the right integration

The **REST Integrations API** reads or changes workspace resources from your server using `x-api-key`. **Webhooks** send events from Bridge to your receiver. **Custom Connections** registers leads from a landing page using its separate public endpoint, `captureKey`, and reCAPTCHA.

An API Key is a server-side secret. A Custom Connections `captureKey` is designed to be in the landing page. These values are not interchangeable. See [Authentication](https://docs.bridge.new/credentials.md) and [Custom Connections](https://docs.bridge.new/lead-capture/index.md).

## People, Agents, and lines

- A **Contact** is the external person your business communicates with. Contact endpoints and external conversation participants refer to this person.
- A **Bridge User** is an internal human user. Internal-user lookup and handoff assignees refer to these users.
- An **Agent** is an automated Agent exposed by the Agents API. Its type is `LEADSCOUT` or `SERVICE_AGENT`; it has its own identifier, availability, and lines.
- A **provider** is a channel type, such as `WHATSAPP`. A **line** is a specific channel used for a conversation. A provider type, phone number, and `providerChannelId` are different values.
- A **workspace** scopes the request. A **brand** is another identifier used where the operation requires or accepts it; it is not a workspace or a line.

A Contact's `ownerId` refers to a Bridge User, not an automated Agent. Resolve it with the [internal-user read endpoint](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/internal-users-api/retrieve-an-internal-user-by-id.md).

## Where each identifier comes from

Use identifiers from the intended workspace. Do not reuse an identifier merely because the same phone number, email, or name appears in another workspace.

| Value you need | Where to obtain or verify it | What to pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | Use the workspace identifier supplied for your integration. If it is missing, ask your Bridge administrator. The published REST contract does not provide a global workspace-list endpoint. | The workspace ID in the operation's path. Custom Connections also requires it in its body and, for browser requests, query string. |
| Contact ID | [Look up a Contact](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/contacts-api/retrieve-a-contact-by-an-identifier.md) by `PHONE`, `EMAIL`, or `ID`; list, create, and upsert responses also return the Contact's `id`. | The returned `id` for `{contactId}` or an identifier object with `identifierType: "ID"`, where that operation accepts it. |
| Bridge User ID | [Look up an internal user](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/internal-users-api/retrieve-an-internal-user-by-an-identifier.md) by `EMAIL` or `ID`, or use the internal-user list. | The returned `id` for `{userId}` or an internal identifier object. Internal-user lookup does not accept `PHONE`. |
| Agent ID | [List Agents](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/agents-api/list-the-agents-of-a-workspace.md). Read `agents[].id`, `type`, and `available`. | `agents[].id` for `{agentId}` in Agent outbound. `available` indicates whether that Agent can start conversations. |
| Agent's line ID | In the same Agents response, read that Agent's `lines[].providerChannelId`. | A line ID belonging to that Agent when the operation accepts `contact.providerChannelId`. Read the outbound reference for line-selection rules. |
| General provider channel | [List provider channels](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/provider-channels-api/get-provider-channels-by-workspace-id.md). This response publishes `provider` and `identifier`, not a channel UUID. | Use these fields only for the purposes documented by the consuming operation. Do not substitute the phone-like `identifier` for `providerChannelId`. |
| `brandId` | An Agent response can expose its `brandId`. For another flow, obtain the intended brand ID from your integration configuration or administrator; the published contract does not provide a general brand-list endpoint. | The brand ID accepted by the operation. A brand ID is not a line ID. |
| `teamId` | Obtain the intended internal team ID from your Bridge administrator or integration configuration. The published REST contract does not provide a team-list endpoint. | The documented team assignment option on conversation creation; do not also supply `participants.internals`. |
| Conversation ID | Create or retrieve a conversation and retain its returned `id`. Outbound responses contain `conversation.id`. | `{conversationId}` or `conversationId`, exactly where the operation requires it. |
| Template | [Discover a template](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/templates-api/discover-a-templates-agnostic-variable-inventory.md) using its ID or name. The response returns `id`, `name`, and variable keys. | Use the selector expected by the sending operation; see the next section. |
| `mediaId` | [Create presigned uploads](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/files-api/create-presigned-uploads-for-files.md). Each response array item has `mediaId` and `presignUrl`. Complete the required PUT upload. | The returned `mediaId` in `mediaIds`, or the media field supported by that operation. Do not send the presigned URL as a media ID. |

**Note**

  Agents lists expose line IDs in the context of each Agent. This is not a general discovery method for every workspace line. If another flow requires a `providerChannelId` you cannot obtain from the published response, ask your Bridge administrator or [support](mailto:support@sainapsis.com) for the intended line ID. Do not generate one or derive one from a telephone number.

## Similar names can require different fields

**Contact lookup** takes query parameters named `type` and `value`. An external participant in a conversation takes `identifier` and `identifierType`, plus the other fields required by that operation. Do not copy a lookup query directly into a participant body.

**Template discovery** accepts an ID or name in the path parameter `{templateId}`. **Conversation onboarding** uses `onboardingTemplates[].templateId`. **Outbound template selection** uses the `template` object's `id` or `name`; read that endpoint's schema rather than renaming every selector to `templateId`.

Use each returned variable's `key` in template `parameters`. Variable keys are not Meta slot indexes. The [template parameters guide](https://docs.bridge.new/templates-and-parameters.md) explains required values, defaults, and the difference between omitted and blank values.

## Keep result identifiers separate

| Returned value | Identifies | What it does not establish by itself |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageId` | A message created through the message endpoint | A provider delivery receipt |
| `trackingId` | An accepted LeadScout handoff request | Completed assignment of the requested users |
| `requestId` | An accepted Custom Connections submission | Delivery of the opening WhatsApp message |
| `eventId` | An identifier supplied with a webhook event; some event families use entity-derived values | A globally unique deduplication key or delivery-order guarantee |

Follow [Receive events](https://docs.bridge.new/webhooks/receive-events.md) for event identity and duplicate handling. See [Responses and errors](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/responses.md) for status codes, asynchronous results, and retry decisions. For a complete flow, follow [your first conversation](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/first-conversation.md) or [sending an attachment](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/send-attachments.md).

Use outbound when an existing Contact should receive an approved WhatsApp template and continue with an AI Agent. Use [create a conversation](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/first-conversation.md) for the general conversation workflow.

## Choose the operation

| Your goal | Operation | How the Agent is selected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start with a specific LeadScout or Service Agent | `POST /bridge/api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/agents/{agentId}/outbound` | You supply the Agent ID from `GET /agents`. |
| Start with a LeadScout selected through the workspace's eligible lines | `POST /bridge/api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/leadscout/outbound` | Bridge resolves the prospecting Agent for the line. |

Both use the REST API host `https://api-connect-us.bridge.new` and a server-side `x-api-key`. They have separate request schemas. Read the [Agents outbound reference](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/agents-api/start-an-outbound-conversation-with-a-contact-as-a-given-agent.md) or [LeadScout outbound reference](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/leadscout-api/initiate-a-leadscout-outbound-conversation-with-a-known-lead.md) for the operation you use.

## Before you send

1. [Look up the Contact](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/contacts-api/retrieve-a-contact-by-an-identifier.md), or [create it](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/contacts-api/create-a-new-contact.md) if missing. Outbound requires a Contact that already exists in the workspace; you do not need to create a separate Conversation or Message first.
2. [List Agents](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/agents-api/list-the-agents-of-a-workspace.md). Choose an available Agent and read its `lines[].providerChannelId`. An AI Agent ID differs from a human Bridge User ID.
3. Choose an approved template. [Discover its variables](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/send-template.md#1-discover-the-variables), supply caller-required values, and check that it is approved for the destination line. Use only the discovery step as this prerequisite; the separate Conversation-creation step in that recipe is not needed for outbound.
4. Confirm that your business has the required opt-in. If you send `consent.status: "GRANTED"`, include `capturedAt`; this records your assertion of consent.

For Agents outbound, `contact.providerChannelId` must belong to the chosen Agent when supplied. It is a preference: another eligible Agent line can be selected. For LeadScout outbound, an explicit line is respected. [Identifiers and their sources](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/identifiers.md) explains which values to use.

## Send a minimal Agent request

Replace every placeholder. This example assumes the chosen template has no unresolved caller-required variables. Set `forceSend` deliberately; the example keeps the default behavior explicit.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body --request POST \
  "https://api-connect-us.bridge.new/bridge/api/v1/workspaces/$WORKSPACE_ID/agents/$AGENT_ID/outbound" \
  --header "x-api-key: $BRIDGE_API_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "contact": {
      "identifier": "f0000001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001",
      "identifierType": "ID",
      "messageProviderType": "WHATSAPP"
    },
    "template": {
      "id": "f0000040-0000-4000-8000-000000000040"
    },
    "forceSend": false
  }'
```

A successful request returns `201`. Store `conversation.id` and interpret these response fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `alreadyInitiated: true` | An existing active conversation was reused. The successful request still adds its new template and follow-ups. |
| `recovered: true` | A released, recoverable conversation was recovered, retaining its ID. Its previous outbound context and `agentContext` are replaced. |
| `additionalMessagesPersisted` | The number of follow-up messages stored. This is not a delivery receipt. |
| `templateSent` | A summary of the opening template stored for sending. Do not interpret the field name as proof of recipient delivery. |

New creation has neither reuse nor recovery set to true. Recovery can happen with `forceSend: false`. Additional messages are persisted in request order; do not rely on a promise that they wait for the Contact to reply. The shared outbound flow persists text follow-ups and does not attach their `mediaIds`. Use the documented `template.media` option for media on the opening template, or the [Message attachment workflow](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/send-attachments.md) for a separate message.

## What forceSend does

Availability is evaluated for **this Contact's conversation on each line**. An occupied line here does not mean the corporate WhatsApp line is globally reserved for one Contact.

The following rules remain subject to Agent availability, template validation, consent validation and session checks.

On a narrow screen, scroll horizontally to compare all four choices. Keyboard users can focus this comparison and use the arrow keys.

| Situation | LeadScout: false | LeadScout: true | Agents: false | Agents: true |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Selected line is free | Create | Create | Create | Create |
| Selected line holds a released conversation marked recoverable | Recover the same ID | Recover the same ID | Recover the same ID | Recover the same ID |
| Automatic selection finds only occupied, active conversations | `409 …0008` | Reuse the first eligible occupied conversation | `409 …0008` | Prefer one controlled by the requested Agent, then apply the controller check below |
| Explicit line is occupied | `409 …0007` | Reuse that conversation | Try other free or recoverable Agent lines; otherwise `409 …0008` | Try other free or recoverable Agent lines; otherwise prefer an occupied line the Agent controls |
| Selected occupied conversation is controlled by a human or another Agent | No active reuse | Legacy route permits reuse, subject to other checks; this does not itself promise a controller transfer | No active reuse | `409 BRIDGE_AI_AGENT_OUTBOUND_0006`; this rejection writes nothing |
| Only blocked or released, nonrecoverable conversations are available | `409 …0008` | `409 …0008` | `409 …0008` | `409 …0008` |

In this table, `…0007` is `BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0007` and `…0008` is `BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0008`. A released conversation is recoverable only when its stored recovery flag permits it; `forceSend` does not make it recoverable.

For both routes, a LeadScout session that is still open and unexpired blocks a new outbound request with `409 BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0017`. Failure to finalize an expired session returns `409 BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0018`. A Service Agent can continue its open, unexpired service session; an expired session is closed before a new one opens.

**Warning**

  `forceSend` is not an idempotency key. Repeating a successful request can add another template and more messages. It does not bypass blocked conversations, session checks, approval rules or validation. A timeout leaves the outcome uncertain: inspect the conversation before deciding whether to submit again.

## Handle conflicts and partial work

| Result | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| `BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0007` / `0008` | Check the Contact's existing conversation and eligible lines. Decide whether reuse is appropriate before enabling `forceSend`. |
| `BRIDGE_AI_AGENT_OUTBOUND_0006` | Inspect `extra.conversationId` and its controller. Coordinate ownership before deliberately releasing it. Do not automatically interrupt a human conversation. |
| `BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0017` / `0018` | Resolve the existing session or contact support. Switching `forceSend` to true does not fix the session. |
| `BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0019` / `0020` / `0021` | Correct missing, conflicting or unknown template variables using discovery. |
| `400 BRIDGE_AI_LEADSCOUT_0016` for an unknown template `mediaId` on Agents outbound | The conversation may already have been created or recovered before this error. Inspect it before retrying. |

[Release conversation](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/conversations-api/release-conversation.md) is a separate operation with business effects. A `204` has no response body. Release only when ending that conversation is your intended action.

## Request a LeadScout handoff to a human

For a LeadScout conversation, resolve the human's [Bridge User ID or email](https://docs.bridge.new/guides/identifiers.md), then call the [manual handoff endpoint](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/leadscout-api/request-a-manual-handoff-of-a-leadscout-conversation-to-internal-users.md). This operation is specific to LeadScout; do not assume it applies to a Service Agent.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body --request POST \
  "https://api-connect-us.bridge.new/bridge/api/v1/workspaces/$WORKSPACE_ID/leadscout/conversations/$CONVERSATION_ID/handoff" \
  --header "x-api-key: $BRIDGE_API_KEY" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "assignees": [
      {"identifier": "f0000002-0000-4000-8000-000000000002", "identifierType": "ID"}
    ]
  }'
```

A `202` acknowledges the request. Save its `trackingId` and `conversationId`; acceptance does not prove that assignment has completed or that a human has read or answered the conversation. The reference does not publish a handoff tracking endpoint, so do not construct one from `trackingId`.

Continue with [error handling](https://docs.bridge.new/error-codes.md) and [webhook receiving](https://docs.bridge.new/webhooks/receive-events.md) to connect this workflow to your system.

pages.title: Create and move pipeline records
pages.description: Create pipeline records for existing Contacts, retry safely with Idempotency-Key, avoid lost updates with expectedRevision, and close or reopen records.
pages.contentMarkdown:
A pipeline record follows one piece of work for a Contact, such as a sales opportunity, through the stages of a pipeline. Use this recipe to keep the records of your system in a Bridge pipeline: create them, change their values, move them between stages, close them with a reason and reopen them. To receive the changes made in Bridge, subscribe to [pipeline record events](https://docs.bridge.new/webhooks/pipeline-records.md).

## Before you start

- Get a server-side API Key from [Authentication](https://docs.bridge.new/credentials.md) and send it in `x-api-key`, as with every other operation. The `workspaceId` in the path must be the workspace of that key. Any other workspace is refused with `403` `BRIDGE_CORE_0301`, and nothing is read or written.
- Pipelines must be enabled for the workspace. Otherwise every operation answers `403` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0301`.
- [Retrieve the pipeline](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/pipelines-api/retrieve-a-pipeline-with-its-stages-and-attributes.md) you write to. It lists the `stageId` values, the attribute ids you use as `values` keys and the active close reasons. [List the pipelines](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/pipelines-api/list-the-pipelines-of-a-workspace.md) to find its id.

```json 403 BRIDGE_CORE_0301
{
  "title": "You do not have permission to access this resource",
  "status": 403,
  "detail": "There exists a mismatch between the claims workspace and the provided workspace",
  "code": "BRIDGE_CORE_0301"
}
```

## The operations

| Your goal | Operation | `Idempotency-Key` | `expectedRevision` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create a record | [`POST .../records`](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/pipeline-records-api/create-a-pipeline-record.md) | Required | Not accepted |
| Find records by your id, a Contact or a pipeline | [`GET .../records`](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/pipeline-records-api/list-pipeline-records.md) | Not accepted | Not accepted |
| Read one record | [`GET .../records/{recordId}`](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/pipeline-records-api/retrieve-a-pipeline-record.md) | Not accepted | Not accepted |
| Change its name or values | [`PATCH .../records/{recordId}`](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/pipeline-records-api/update-a-pipeline-record.md) | Not accepted | Optional |
| Move it to another stage, or close it | [`POST .../records/{recordId}/move`](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/pipeline-records-api/move-a-pipeline-record-to-another-stage.md) | Required | Optional |
| Reopen a closed record | [`POST .../records/{recordId}/reopen`](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/pipeline-records-api/reopen-a-closed-pipeline-record.md) | Required | Optional |

`...` stands for `/bridge/api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}`, on the REST API host `https://api-connect-us.bridge.new`.

## Create a record

Name the Contact with exactly one of `contact.id`, `contact.phone` or `contact.email`. Bridge finds the Contact the same way as [contact lookup](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/contacts-api/retrieve-a-contact-by-an-identifier.md); a Contact merged into another one resolves to the Contact that replaced it. The Contact is never created: when it does not exist the request fails with `404` `BRIDGE_EXTERNAL_0001`, so [create the Contact](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/contacts-api/create-a-new-contact.md) first and retry.

Without `pipelineId` the record goes to the workspace's default pipeline, and without `stageId` to the pipeline's initial stage. A final stage is refused at creation. A pipeline set not to accept records from the API refuses the creation with `403` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0317`.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body --request POST \
  "https://api-connect-us.bridge.new/bridge/api/v1/workspaces/$WORKSPACE_ID/records" \
  --header "x-api-key: $BRIDGE_API_KEY" \
  --header "Idempotency-Key: erp-opp-981-create" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "contact": {
      "phone": "+573001234567"
    }
  }'
```

A created record answers `201` with a `Location` header and the record. Keep its `id` and its `revision`:

```json 201
{
  "id": "record-1",
  "pipelineId": "pipe-sales",
  "pipelineVersion": 3,
  "stageId": "stage-new",
  "state": "OPEN",
  "name": "Ana Gómez",
  "values": {
    "budget": 1500
  },
  "contact": {
    "id": "contact-1"
  },
  "ownerId": null,
  "source": "API",
  "externalId": null,
  "revision": 1,
  "closeReason": null,
  "closedAt": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-11-11T15:00:00.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-11-11T15:00:00.000Z"
}
```

```json 404 BRIDGE_EXTERNAL_0001
{
  "title": "The requested external user was not found",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "External user was not found with PHONE and value +573001234567",
  "code": "BRIDGE_EXTERNAL_0001",
  "extra": {
    "externalIdentificationType": "PHONE",
    "externalIdentificationValue": "+573001234567"
  }
}
```

### Link the record to your own id

Send `externalId` with the id the record has in your system. A pipeline holds **one record per `externalId`**: a second creation with the same `externalId` in the same pipeline fails with `409` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0003`, and `extra.recordId` is the record that already has it. Read that record instead of creating another one. To find it later, [list records](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/pipeline-records-api/list-pipeline-records.md) with `externalId` (and `pipelineId` when it is not the default pipeline).

The record id is chosen by Bridge; the request body has no field to set it.

```json 409 BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0003
{
  "title": "A record with this external id already exists in the pipeline",
  "status": 409,
  "code": "BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0003",
  "extra": {
    "recordId": "record-1",
    "pipelineId": "pipe-sales",
    "externalId": "ERP-1"
  }
}
```

### One open record per Contact

A pipeline can be set in Bridge to allow a Contact only one open record at a time. In such a pipeline, creating a record for a Contact that already has an open one fails with `409` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0318`, and `extra.openRecordId` is that open record: work on it instead. Closed records do not count, so a Contact can start a new record once the previous one is closed. Reopening a record fails the same way when the Contact has another open record in the pipeline.

```json 409 BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0318
{
  "title": "The contact already has an open record in this pipeline",
  "status": 409,
  "detail": "Contact 'contact-1' already has the open record 'record-open' in pipeline 'pipe-onboarding'",
  "code": "BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0318",
  "extra": {
    "openRecordId": "record-open",
    "pipelineId": "pipe-onboarding",
    "externalUserId": "contact-1"
  }
}
```

## Retry safely with Idempotency-Key

`POST .../records`, `POST .../move` and `POST .../reopen` require an `Idempotency-Key` header of 1 to 255 characters. Use one key per change you want to make, and send the same key when you retry that change.

| You send | Bridge answers |
| --- | --- |
| The same key and the same body, after the first request finished | The same status (`201` or `200`) with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The body is the record **as it is now**, so it can already show later changes |
| The same key with a different body, or on another record or operation | `422` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0402` |
| The same key while the first request is still running | `409` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0401`. Retry after a pause |
| The same key after the first request failed | The request runs again: a failed request frees its key |

A key is kept for **24 hours**; after that the same key runs as a new request. Keys are shared by every operation of the workspace, so do not reuse one across records.

**Warning**

  If a request is cut off before it finishes, its key can keep answering `409` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0401` for up to 24 hours. Retry with a new key. Send `externalId` when you create records, so that a retry with a new key can never create a second record.

## Avoid overwriting changes with expectedRevision

Every record has a `revision` that goes up by one each time the record changes. Send the `revision` you last read as `expectedRevision` in the body of `PATCH`, `move` or `reopen`. If someone changed the record in the meantime, the request fails with `409` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0101` and changes nothing. `extra.currentRecord` is the record as it is now: decide again from it and retry with its `revision`.

`expectedRevision` is optional. Without it, the change applies to the record as Bridge reads it, and a change made at the same moment can still fail it with the same `409`.

```json PATCH
{
  "expectedRevision": 2,
  "name": "Renamed"
}
```

```json 409 BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0101
{
  "title": "The pipeline record was modified by another operation",
  "status": 409,
  "detail": "Pipeline record 'record-1' is at revision 4, the write expected 2",
  "code": "BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0101",
  "extra": {
    "recordId": "record-1",
    "expectedRevision": 2,
    "currentRevision": 4,
    "currentRecord": {
      "id": "record-1",
      "stageId": "stage-proposal",
      "revision": 4
    }
  }
}
```

`extra.currentRecord` holds the whole record, with the same fields as the `201` response above; the example shows only three of them.

## Move, close and reopen

[Move the record](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/pipeline-records-api/move-a-pipeline-record-to-another-stage.md) with the `stageId` of a stage of the pipeline version it follows. Moving it to a **final stage closes it**. A move to a final stage can carry `reasonId`, one of the active close reasons of the pipeline, and a `reasonNote` of up to 500 characters, which needs `reasonId`. The close reason is optional: without one, the record closes with `closeReason: null`.

```bash
curl --fail-with-body --request POST \
  "https://api-connect-us.bridge.new/bridge/api/v1/workspaces/$WORKSPACE_ID/records/$RECORD_ID/move" \
  --header "x-api-key: $BRIDGE_API_KEY" \
  --header "Idempotency-Key: erp-opp-981-won" \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "stageId": "stage-won",
    "reasonId": "reason-price"
  }'
```

The answer is `200` with the record. A closed record has `state: "FINAL"`, `closedAt` and, when the move carried one, `closeReason` with the `id`, `label` and `note` of the reason.

| Problem | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| The record is already in that stage | `409` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0004` |
| The record is closed | `409` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0306`: reopen it first |
| The stage is not in the record's pipeline version | `422` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0311`, with `errRecordStage` in `extra.errors` |
| A close reason or note on a move to an open stage | `422` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0311`, with `errReasonOnlyFinal` in `extra.errors` |
| The close reason does not exist, or is retired | `422` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0315`, or `422` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0314` |
| The stage requires a complete Contact | `422` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0305`; `extra.missing` names what the Contact lacks |

[Reopen a closed record](https://docs.bridge.new/api-reference/pipeline-records-api/reopen-a-closed-pipeline-record.md) to take it back to the open stage it was in before it was closed; its close reason is cleared. When its history names no open stage of its version, the record goes to the pipeline's initial stage. The body is optional and only takes `expectedRevision`. Reopening an open record fails with `409` `BRIDGE_PIPELINE_0307`.

## Stage actions run on every entry

**Warning**

  A stage can have actions, such as creating a task or creating a record in another pipeline. They run **every time a record enters the stage**: when it is created in the stage, when it is moved to it and when it is reopened into it. That includes every record you create through the API, so a bulk import into a stage with actions runs them once per record. Check the actions of the stage before an import.

The actions run after the API answers; the response does not wait for them. Their results arrive as [`pipeline_action.*` webhook events](https://docs.bridge.new/webhooks/pipeline-records.md#stage-action-events).

## Errors and limits

- Every error answers a `Problem` body. Branch on `code`, not on `title`. See [Pipeline error codes](https://docs.bridge.new/error-codes.md#pipeline-error-codes) for each code and what to do.
- The pipelines operations draw from the same budget as the rest of the API: **50 requests every 5 seconds per workspace**. See [Rate limits](https://docs.bridge.new/rate-limits.md).
